title: Soil Formation
ques: Soil doesn't just appear overnight. Explain briefly how big rocks slowly turn into the soil we use for planting seeds.

answer.content: Big rocks are slowly broken down into tiny pieces over many, many years by things like the wind, rain, sun, and flowing water. This process is called **weathering**. The tiny rock pieces mix with dead leaves and bugs to become soil.

explanation: This exercise covers the geological process of weathering and soil formation.

title: Types of Soil
ques: If you pour water onto sandy soil, it drains very quickly. If you pour it onto clay soil, it sits on top and becomes sticky. Which type of soil is usually best for growing most garden plants, and why?

answer.content: **Loam** soil is usually the best. It is a mix of sand, clay, and lots of dead plant material (humus). It is best because it holds enough water for the plants to drink, but drains well enough so the roots don't rot.

explanation: This tests practical application of soil properties for agriculture.

title: Soil Conservation
ques: Why is it helpful for farmers to plant trees or thick grass around the edges of their crop fields?

answer.content: Planting trees or grass helps stop **soil erosion**. The roots hold the topsoil tightly together so that it does not get blown away by strong winds or washed away by heavy rain.

explanation: This introduces environmental conservation and sustainable farming practices.
